what_it_does: This paper surveys data compression practices across nine domains of scientific computing (like climate modeling, physics simulation, biology) running on supercomputers. Scientific researchers compress enormous datasets to save storage and transfer time, but compress them in ways that lose information (lossy compression). The paper documents which compression methods scientists actually use, what properties they care about (compression speed, how much data loss they tolerate), and whether compression tools available today actually support those needs, revealing gaps between what's available and what scientists require.
